background.problemStatement: The current ChartPanel has layout bugs: (1) toggling RSI visibility causes volume bars and X-axis to be pushed out of view, (2) RSI panel shows stale data when switching tickers, (3) volume toggle adds unnecessary complexity.
background.rootCause: The bug is in _render_chart() height calculation. When RSI is visible, code does: available_height = self.size.height - 7 - volume_height - rsi_height. But RSI is NOT inside #chart-content - it's yielded separately in compose(). So the chart area shrinks but RSI panel then ADDS 7 more rows below it, causing overflow.

currentArchitecture.height_calculation: Incorrectly subtracts RSI height from chart area when RSI is actually ADDED as sibling

criticalBugAnalysis.occlusion_root_cause: In _render_chart(), line ~295: 'rsi_height = 7 if self.is_rsi_visible() else 0' then 'available_height = self.size.height - 7 - volume_height - rsi_height'. But RSI panel is yielded from compose() as a SIBLING to #chart-content, not inside it. So shrinking chart-content doesn't make room - Textual just stacks RSI below, causing overflow.
criticalBugAnalysis.fix_approach: Remove rsi_height from the calculation. RSI panel stacks naturally as a sibling via Textual's layout model.

criticalLearningsFromAgentsMd: NEVER use ANSI escape codes for colors in Textual widgets - use Rich markup ([green]text[/green])
Label widgets need markup=True to render Rich markup colors
Textual CSS height: auto and 1fr can conflict - prefer explicit heights for predictable layout
Widget compose() defines structure, _render_content() updates dynamic content
Use container.remove_children() + mount() pattern for dynamic updates

textualLayoutModel.compose_yields: Creates persistent widget tree, siblings stack vertically by default
textualLayoutModel.key_insight: RSI panel yielded from compose() is a SIBLING that stacks BELOW, not space reserved inside
textualLayoutModel.height_management: Don't subtract sibling heights - Textual handles stacking automatically
